text: 'athena backtest' now passes on the real records, but its evidence is wrong, so the pass is false confidence. Fix the three root causes. (1) Evidence must postdate the decision: D87 reached main at 2026-10-13T19:21Z (commit 383edca, PR #41), yet it cites interventions 20261013-150702-kn3q (15:07Z) and 20261013-162049-qk2d (16:20Z), which predate it. Take a decision's start time from the history of its text, and count only later records. (2) Derivation matched the word 'merged' anywhere: kn3q's 422 came from opening a PR (the wrong-base bug), and 'merged' there describes the operator's own action. Derive a merge refusal only when the text ties the HTTP code to the refused merge itself; when unsure, derive nothing. (3) The pass conditions checked counts and that ids exist, not that each citation is valid. Make the backtest validate each cited record against the signal's fields and time window, and fail when any citation is invalid. Expected on the real records: D87 under review citing only ar1x, both directly and through its derived record; the introspection record names ar1x's event; nothing else is flagged. Report the real result either way.
